definition: A sequence architecture family (S4, Mamba) that processes tokens through a learned recurrent dynamical system with linear-time computation and constant-size state, making very long sequences cheap.
details: A sequence architecture family (S4, Mamba) that processes tokens through a learned recurrent dynamical system with linear-time computation and constant-size state, making very long sequences cheap.

explainer.lead: State space models are a sequence architecture family that processes tokens through a learned recurrent dynamical system. They matter because they give linear-time computation and a constant-size state, making very long sequences cheap.

tiers.eli5: Instead of re-reading the whole book each time you turn a page, you keep a running summary in your head and update it as you go.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers reach for them when context is very long and attention cost becomes prohibitive. A pitfall is that a fixed-size state must compress history, which can lose detail.
tiers.paperLevel: The family includes S4 and Mamba; tokens pass through a learned recurrent dynamical system with linear-time computation and constant-size state. The known limit is the constant-size state's capacity to retain information.

explainer.example: A model using a constant-size running state scans a very long document in linear time rather than comparing every token pair.
